findings.issue_text: packages/core/EventManager.ts:119 — mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` is dereferenced without optional chaining, so any Google Meet booking whose organizer/event type has no destination calendar throws TypeError and 500s the whole booking.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:592 — The `console.error(message)` was deleted from updateAllCalendarEvents' catch, so a total reschedule/update failure now produces zero logs while still returning results the caller treats as normal.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:344 — prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id: destination.credentialId } })` is unscoped by user/team, so any credentialId stored on a member's DestinationCalendar row causes the server to decrypt and use that credential to write calendar events outside the organizer's credential set.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:542 — credential` can still be undefined after the DB fallback (missing app.slug); `updateEvent(undefined, ...)` rejects, `Promise.all` rejects, and the catch marks every host calendar reference as failed even though the other hosts' updates already went through.

goldens.comment: A null reference occurs in GoogleCalendarService.createEvent() and updateEvent() when mainHostDestinationCalendar is destructured from evt.destinationCalendar but evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array, causing mainHostDestinationCalendar to be undefined.
The optional chaining on mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration is redundant since you already check mainHostDestinationCalendar in the ternary condition.

Logic error: when externalCalendarId is provided, you're searching for a calendar where externalId === externalCalendarId, but this will always fail since you're looking for a calendar that matches itself. Should likely find by credentialId or use different logic.

Logic inversion in organization creation: The slug property is now conditionally set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, instead of when it's false as originally intended. This change, combined with requestedSlug still being set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, results in both properties being set when billing is enabled, and neither when disabled

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:147 — The new per-host `cal.credentialId === credentialId` match silently falls back to "primary" when no destination matches the credential, and there is no GoogleCalendarService test asserting each host's event lands on that host's externalId.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:256 — externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` can only ever resolve to undefined in the else branch, and no updateEvent test exists to catch the dead lookup.

adjudication.rationale:
Yes. In GoogleCalendarService.updateEvent (and similarly deleteEvent), the fallback logic is:

```ts
const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId
  ? externalCalendarId
  : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;
```

When the else-branch runs, `externalCalendarId` is falsy/undefined by definition, so the `.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` is effectively searching for `cal.externalId === undefined`. In normal data this will not match anything, so it resolves to `undefined`, meaning the code loses the intended destination calendar and may fall back to an incorrect calendarId downstream.

The part of the finding claiming “no updateEvent test exists” is not verifiable from this diff, but the dead/incorrect lookup itself is a real correctness bug introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:317 — deleteEvent repeats the same self-contradictory find, so cancellation without an explicit externalCalendarId always falls back to "primary"; no deleteEvent test covers it.

adjudication.rationale: In packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts the updated deleteEvent logic computes `calendarId` as `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`. When `externalCalendarId` is undefined/null, the `.find(...)` compares `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` (i.e., against undefined/null), which will almost always return no match, yielding `undefined`. The call then falls back to `defaultCalendarId` ("primary"), so deletions without an explicit `externalCalendarId` will target the primary calendar even if `event.destinationCalendar` contains a valid externalId. That is a real correctness bug introduced by this diff. The claim about no tests covering it is not directly verifiable from the shown diff, but the deletion-selection bug itself is.
